backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:884 — oauth_token_refresh awaits llm_document_repo.update_voice_device_tokens (WHERE id=$1 AND is_active=TRUE, fetch_optional) but only handles the Err arm via map_err; an Ok(None) (device deactivated between find and update) is discarded, then the handler logs 'Successfully refreshed OAuth tokens' and returns VoiceTokenRefreshResult { success: true }. Meanwhile oauth_manager.refresh_token already rotated the upstream token at line 808, so the new access/refresh pair is never persisted — the caller believes rotation succeeded while the device row still holds the pre-rotation refresh token (which Amazon/Google may treat as revoked). Handle Ok(None) explicitly: 404 or fail-loud 500 so the false-success + stale-token state is caught.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/government_portal.rs:549,623,699 — validate_submission, submit_submission, and cancel_submission each end with `let _ = state.government_portal_repo.create_audit(CreateSubmissionAudit { ... }).await;` with no tracing::warn on error. These are regulatory-submission audit-trail writes (SubmissionStatus::Validated / Submitted / Cancelled) for a government portal integration. On any transient DB failure the audit row is silently missing — no operator signal, no retry, no fallback log — leaving compliance gaps invisible. Log the error at minimum; ideally make audit persistence transactional with the status change.
